changes: Kedumbāṭa: confidence lowered from high to medium, because the text is a fragment and the word could be a title or designation rather than a personal name. His role is kept as official, since he was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to the work.
place.normalized cleared: Viṣṇupādukā hill is in the northern Kathmandu Valley, but no modern place is certain enough to give.
Notes expanded: the lacuna 'śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ' may read śrīpādair ... agrajaḥ ('elder brother'), and the king (śrīpādaiḥ) and queen (devyāḥ) are not named.

notes: This is a fragmentary, undated inscription (DV 8) on a column near a water conduit on Viṣṇupādukā hill. Kedumbāṭa was appointed (niyojitaḥ) to start the work on the stone pillar, apparently by royal order (śrīpādaiḥ). The king is not named. The queen (devyāḥ, 'for the queen' or 'of the goddess') is not named either. The lacuna 'śrīpādai . . . grajaḥ' may hide a word ending in -agrajaḥ ('elder brother'). If so, someone named in the lost text is described as an elder brother, possibly Kedumbāṭa himself, but this cannot be checked. 'Kedumbāṭa' is taken as a personal name, but it is not certain.
